name: Oregano
grown_as: Oregano, the same plant as our native wild marjoram, a hardy perennial. The library also lists Marjoram and Wild marjoram; sweet marjoram (Origanum majorana) is a different, tender plant with grey leaves and white flowers. Golden oregano ('Aureum') has yellow leaves. Drawn as the green, pink-flowered plant. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A bushy clump 30 to 60 cm high of upright, reddish, hairy, square stems that branch near the top, from a creeping, woody-based rootstock.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite, in pairs, each pair at right angles to the one below
leaf.outline: Small, broadly oval, 1 to 4 cm long
leaf.margin: Smooth, or with a few very small shallow teeth
leaf.veins: A midrib and 3 to 4 faint side veins each side
leaf.surface: Softly hairy, dotted with tiny oil glands (seen against the light); paler beneath

flower.petals: Joined; short upper lip, three-lobed lower lip
flower.centre: Stamens sticking out of the tube
flower.behind: Each flower sits against an oval, overlapping bract, dark red-purple, so the heads look purple even before they open
flower.carried: In dense short spikes gathered into a loose, flat-topped or domed, branched head at the top of each stem
flower.size: Flowers 4 to 7 mm; the head 3 to 10 cm across

fruit: The heads dry brown with the bracts still on, holding tiny nutlets. Seeds: tiny brown seeds, round to oval, about 0.5 mm, like dust.
seedling: Two tiny round seed leaves; then tiny oval, opposite, softly hairy true leaves.
winter: The flowering stems die back; a low mat of small rounded leaves, often purple-tinged, stays at the base.

leaf: a small broad oval leaf on a short stalk
edge smooth or with only tiny shallow teeth
bloom: many tiny pink-purple flowers in dense short spikes
dark red-purple bracts showing among them
spikes gathered into a flat-topped head
young: a low leafy clump of small oval leaves in pairs
crop: a bushy clump of upright reddish stems with small oval leaves in pairs
flower: flat-topped branched heads of pink-purple flowers with dark purple bracts on top of the stems
seedhead: dry brown flat-topped heads on the old stems
dormant: a low mat of small rounded leaves, some purple-tinged, at the soil

look_alikes: Sweet marjoram has grey hairy leaves and white flowers in small knot-like heads. Thyme has much smaller, narrower leaves on woody stems. Wild basil (Clinopodium vulgare) carries its pink flowers in separated rings with bristly calyces, not in a flat head.
